13: Why each dish carries a method
14: The methods seeded in the example follow a rule: plate cost of $6 or more, target margin; $2 or less, perceived value; the rest of the mains, market price; everything else, cost factor. The factor only works in the middle band: on the ribeye it sends the price through the roof, and on a dessert it leaves it below what the guest would pay. The target margin (method B) is seeded in DOLLARS PER CATEGORY ($6.50 starters, $10.50 mains, $4.20 desserts) — the weighted average contribution margin of the menu, not a multiple of the cost: that's why the ribeye comes out at $25.30 (14.80 + 10.50) and not $49.33, and its food cost lands above target instead of off the chart. Market price and perceived value carry their own spread per dish (between 5% and 25% over the current menu price, depending on how different each dish is from the competition), not a single factor for the whole menu.

Amounts carry no currency symbol: they are in your currency. Tax on the menu price by market (cell "Tax rate (%)", 0% by default):
• US: menu prices are pre-tax and sales tax is added on the bill. Leave 0%.
